# Independent audit of actual residual-tail and triangle-scale transfer

Read all four sections of `candidate 111d4eb988c37817`. **PASS**, with no repair identified.

The nonempty strict residual corner has positive area even if its initially selected point lies on the boundary of A: a small movement toward an interior point preserves all strict inequalities. Balanced normals place that corner in the same actual shifted tail at gap W>0. The original proper section is differentiable under threshold movement, and the concave cap-root tangent at zero has the sign used in (1). It is an upper tangent, so it gives an upper bound on the original section. The positive shifted tail and a positive slab justify both strict inequalities `0<T_i<U_i` and `sigma_Ai<2U_i/W`.

The actual triangle area identity has the correct determinant factor. In two-normal coordinates the three origin determinants are precisely the three terms `a_i a_j-b_ij b_ji`; their sum is twice the normalized area. The signed-row identities give `R=4-sum f_i^2=8Dk/H^2`. The lower bound `R>201/400` follows with the exact displayed constants from F>59/20 and the sum of all three Lorentz inequalities.

The support triangle belongs to the same B and same balanced normals, so its area `W^2/(2D)` cannot be independently normalized away. Combining it with the actual K identity yields exactly `H/W<=2/sqrt(beta R)`. Substitution of the coarea section formula introduces no lost factor: the resulting coefficient in (6) is exactly the displayed one. The common-budget substitutions in (7) retain the actual three correlated cap masses.

Finally, bounding the other two terms in the mixed-weight denominator by their ordinary weights gives (8) in the correct direction. At lambda=223/1000, the sufficient ratio is exactly `(9lambda-2)/(4(1-lambda))=7/3108`. The source correctly makes no assertion that its new upper bound forces this ratio in all configurations, and does not apply the present-corner lemma to an absent corner by merely substituting a zero lower tail estimate.

## Independent audit of the completed Sections 5–6

Read the subsequently appended mixed transfer theorem and shell-descent corollary in full. **PASS**, with no correction identified. The original limited transfer discussion is now completed only under the additional explicit hypotheses in Section 5.

The common actual budgets first supply `Q>=4k/9`, hence k<=a+b. The bad-source and nonheavy hypotheses and a<b/32 then give precisely alpha<1/31, beta>30/31 and r<128/279. The actual triangular-middle incidence and barycentric argument justify every q_i>20/49. The eta_i calculation has the correct strictness: all eta_i>0, so their squared sum is strictly smaller than the square of their sum. This gives `sum q_i>65/49` and the exact upper bound `Delta<80/4557`.

The overlap surplus E is nonnegative because the three A caps actually cover the plane. The inequality `U_i-sqrt(U_i delta_i)<=E` holds in both delta_i statuses; no absent residual is used to justify the strict shifted-tail premise. Combining it with the same B support scale gives (12). The passage to (13) uses the exact mixed weights, all other section ratios being nonnegative, together with the lower and upper bounds on sqrt(q_i); all denominator comparisons have the stated directions.

The rational upper bound on x is strictly below 3/4 and has a positive denominator. This relaxed upper bound still suffices to force the two other f values above `(s/rho)x`. The constrained square-root tangent retains the actual cap-sum slack, with the correct sign on the two nonpositive differences q_j-c. Its consequences `67/100<x<3/4` and `Delta<=2rho B(x)/x` are valid. The derivative bound B'<1/10 and the bound `4rho/(mL)<6` then control the endpoint-section penalty exactly as (17).

For the reciprocal secant estimate, the nonconstant numerator before replacing t by s is positive on the entire stated interval; thus both occurrences of t may be increased without reversing the estimate. The derivative of zeta is exactly (19). Its strictly negative numerator and the upper bound on its positive denominator give the stated bound `zeta'<-328/75<-4`. The positive final product bound proves p_i>2/9, including the hypothetical equality case. Only the chosen present corner invokes the shifted-tail estimate.

For Section 6, the cited genuine-criticality gauge theorem supplies the pair-weight floor. Singleton signatures of positive measure correspond to present strict residual corners; null boundary signatures are harmless. The finite set of signatures therefore gives a single tau>2/9 on almost all of A. Contracting about any p in A removes an actual nested shell, and integration gives the derivative estimate (21). Proper cap sections make the threshold functions continuously differentiable near the original parameters, including contraction centers on the boundary of A.

The meeting-point Jacobian is invertible by the balanced normals and positive section coefficients. Its normalized inverse coefficients are exactly the p_i used in the shell estimate, so the derivative Q'_0 has no missing factor. The three new middle traces cover every point, giving an all-source upper bound Q_t. Both strict endpoint gaps are explicitly needed and retained; set inclusion controls every endpoint point after contraction. The normalized upper bound decreases strictly, and the convex hull of the three lifted fibers has exactly the advertised integer fibers because the new midpoint contribution remains in K. Thus the variation is an actual convex-body variation.

Reran `supporting computation verify_present_corner_mixed_transfer_defect_transport.py`: **1,493 exact geometry and transfer checks PASS**. The result remains confined to triangular K, the stated actual common caps, a<b/32 and the other bad-source/nonheavy premises; the extremizer exclusion additionally needs genuine criticality, global Q, and both strict endpoint gaps.
